newsitem.title: USA: U.S. outlines global warming economic analyses.
newsitem.headline: U.S. outlines global warming economic analyses.

text.p: The Clinton administration will use three different types of economic models to forecast how policies to curb global warming would affect the economy, a top Commerce Department official said on Friday.

In a news briefing, Under Secretary for Economic Affairs Ev Ehrlich outlined the steps the administration was taking in preparing economic impact analyses that will help form the U.S. stance in international talks on cutting industrial pollution.
The economic analyses are to be ready in June, and the administration this summer is to propose targets and timetables for reducing emissions from burning fossil fuels.

Ehrlich said economists would use a short-term model that measures the economy by quarters, a longer-term model that measures it in five-year intervals, and a model that makes assumptions on technological advances and their economic impacts.
"Between the three models, we have a pretty rich set of tools," he said.
The analyses should show how different regions of the country and industrial sectors would be affected by various targets and timetables, he said.
Ehrlich said the analyses would not reflect economic benefits of slowing climate change because those would be uncertain and are "best expressed as insurance benefits."
But he said the analyses could measure known benefits such as cleaner air that meets federal quality standards, reductions in illnesses, hospitalizations and other measurable costs.
The analyses will be reviewed by 12 economists who will act as individual adviser instead as a panel, Ehrlich said.

While it has not yet suggested targets for reducing pollution, the administration has proposed an international system of buying and selling pollution allowances as way to create incentives to reduce emissions.
